overview: Physically, a continuous rotation servo looks identical to a standard hobby servo and uses the exact same 3-wire PWM signal — but internally its position-sensing potentiometer has been removed or disconnected, so instead of driving to a fixed angle and holding, the same PWM pulse now controls speed and direction, spinning continuously like a geared motor. That makes it a popular 'motor plus built-in driver' shortcut for simple wheeled robots: no separate motor driver IC needed, just plug into a PWM pin the same way you would for a normal servo. The tradeoff is that it has no positional feedback at all — you can't ask it 'what angle are you at,' only 'spin this fast, this direction.'
simpleSummary: A servo motor modified to spin continuously like a wheel motor instead of stopping at an angle.

specifications.controlSignal: PWM, 50 Hz, same as a standard servo
specifications.speedControl: Pulse width above/below neutral controls speed and direction, not angle

pinMap.name: Signal (orange/yellow wire)
pinMap.function: PWM pulse — width above ~1.5ms spins one direction, below spins the other, with speed proportional to distance from neutral.
pinMap.gotcha: Unlike a positional servo, sending write(90) with the Arduino Servo library does NOT mean '90 degrees' — it means 'stop' (or close to it); the exact stop point usually needs manual calibration per unit.

pinMap.name: VCC (red wire)
pinMap.currentLimit: Depends on load, can spike under stall
pinMap.gotcha: Same multi-servo power rule as any hobby servo — don't power more than one directly from a microcontroller's 5V pin.

useCases.title: Simple wheeled robot drive wheel
useCases.scenario: Skip a separate motor driver entirely — wire two continuous rotation servos straight to PWM pins for a simple differential-drive robot.

useCases.title: Conveyor or rotating display
useCases.scenario: Continuous, speed-controllable rotation without needing an H-bridge motor driver.

oftenConfusedWith: Standard positional servos (SG90/MG996R) — same wiring, completely different control behavior
oftenUpgradedTo: DC geared motor + motor driver (more torque/speed control options, at the cost of needing a separate driver IC)
